advisors.name: Yulia Tsvetkov
areas: AI ethics and equitable language technology
advisors.match_reason: Tsvetkov's lab is the single strongest match. MAGNET (NeurIPS 2024) directly addresses multilingual tokenizer unfairness via adaptive gradient-based tokenization — precisely the applicant's interest in tokenizer adaptation for low-resource languages. Voices Unheard (EMNLP 2024) builds NLP resources for under-resourced dialects (Yorùbá), methodologically identical to what the applicant wants for Indian languages. Teaching LLMs to Abstain across Languages (EMNLP 2024) and Trusting Your Evidence (NAACL 2024, W4401042371) directly address multilingual faithfulness and context-grounded evaluation — core interests 2 and 3. Her stated lab goal is 'NLP for All: extend language technology beyond narrow populations and across linguistic and cultural boundaries.'

advisors.name: Hannaneh Hajishirzi
advisors.match_reason: Hajishirzi leads the H2Lab and co-directs the OLMo/Dolma open LLM effort. OLMo (ACL 2024, W4402671236) and Dolma (ACL 2024, W4402671286) are foundational open model+data infrastructure on which efficient adaptation and data-selection research (interest 1) can be built. Her lab's work on RAG (W7127589252, Nature 2025) directly maps to the applicant's secondary interest in retrieval-augmented generation for government/health information. MatFormer (NeurIPS 2024, on her lab page) addresses elastic/nested inference — relevant to on-device model compression. Her H2Lab page explicitly states goals around making AI 'efficient and effective', and she co-advises students with Tsvetkov on multilingual topics.

advisors.name: Noah A. Smith
areas: Data selection and quality for LLMs
advisors.match_reason: Smith's ARK group has a strong track record on multilingual NLP evaluation and data quality — the paper 'Whose Language Counts as High Quality? Measuring Language Ideologies in Text Data Selection' (visible on his S2 page) is directly relevant to low-resource language data selection (interest 1). He co-authored MAGNET (tokenizer fairness) and Voices Unheard (Yorùbá dialects) with Tsvetkov, and co-directs the OLMo open LLM effort, making him a natural co-advisor for students working on efficient LLM adaptation. His explicit focus on 'evaluation that matters' (his bio says 'he also works on core problems of research methodology like evaluation') aligns with interest 2. The Noah's ARK page notes an open undergraduate/master research interest form, suggesting openness to new students.

advisors.name: Luke Zettlemoyer
advisors.match_reason: Zettlemoyer's group produced QLoRA (NeurIPS 2023 oral), the seminal parameter-efficient fine-tuning method that is the backbone of adapting large models to low-resource settings — directly relevant to interest 1. He co-contributed to OLMo and Dolma (ACL 2024 best paper awards) and supervised a thesis on 'Towards Large Language Models for Everyone: Instruction Following, Knowledge Retrieval and Multilingualism' (Victoria Lin, 2024). His current student Sneha Kudugunta, listed on his group page, works on multilingual models. His profile page explicitly states 'I admit students every year.'

advisors.name: Kurtis Heimerl
advisors.match_reason: Heimerl's focus is Computing for Development, which superficially connects to deploying language technology in underserved communities. However, his recent 2024–2026 papers (W4401176673 dAuth cellular auth, W4415250212 smart tech for homeless shelters, W7154079896 on-device AI for conservation) are about mobile infrastructure and community technology — not NLP, speech, or Indian-language modeling. His work does not engage with low-resource NLP, multilingual LLMs, or any of the applicant's core interests.
